sobre_destaque: The research group Observatório de Universos Bíblicos (Observatory of Biblical Universes, OUB) investigates religious phenomena, practices and productions in the historical and cultural contexts in which biblical texts were conceived, produced and first received, through the lens and tools of religious studies.
sobre_paragrafos: Traditionally tied to Christian exegesis and theology, the study of biblical traditions has been subjected to an increasingly frequent conceptual and methodological cross-pollination with other academic fields. Yet, while this new configuration has blurred old disciplinary boundaries and brought previously neglected bodies of evidence back into the spotlight, it still lacks the conceptual framework needed to address the resulting epistemological destabilization.

Within this scenario, the group articulates research that examines inscriptions, images, objects, literature, and rituals of religions within the biblical universe, drawing on questions, methodologies, and conceptual frameworks from anthropology, archaeology, hermeneutics, history, literature, philosophy, and the sociology of religion.

focos.titulo: Material and visual mediations of biblical religions
focos.texto: Investigates how artefacts from the contexts in which biblical texts were conceived, produced and first received mediated religious ideas and practices in the ancient Southern Levant. Brings together research that examines inscriptions, images and objects of the biblical universes through the questions, tools and conceptual frameworks of the anthropology, archaeology, hermeneutics, philosophy, history and literature of religion.

focos.titulo: Social and literary mediations of biblical religions
focos.texto: Investigates how (para)biblical texts from the contexts in which biblical texts were conceived, produced and first received mediated religious ideas and practices. Brings together research that examines inscriptions, literatures and rites of the biblical universes through the questions, tools and conceptual frameworks of the anthropology, hermeneutics, philosophy, history, literature and sociology of religion.

Investigates how scholars of the contexts in which biblical texts were conceived, produced and first received mediate the concept of religion. Brings together research that examines the aesthetics of reception and the history of interpretation and of research on the biblical universes through the questions, tools and conceptual frameworks of the anthropology, hermeneutics, history, literature and sociology of religion.
